edits.old: The `remove(key)` method does NOT block waiting for background write-through to complete. It proceeds immediately with removal.
edits.new: The `remove(key)` method does NOT block waiting for background write-through to complete. It proceeds immediately with removal. *(Sync 2026-10-14, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-clear-mt` — code authoritative, commit `0236a3c98`. Before it, a `remove` that came before the key's write-through had run returned `KeyNotFound` and left the entry cached, because the dispatch map refused the read pin the write-through holds.)* The dispatcher MUST record, per key, the read pin that `copy_gpu_to_memory_completed` leaves on the entry for its background write-through (`WriteThroughPins`). The record MUST be made before the job is enqueued, so the job cannot start first. When `dm.remove` refuses with `ActiveReferences` and that recorded pin is held, `remove` MUST take the pin over: it releases the pin and removes the dispatch-map entry. If another reader still holds the key, the pin is given back and `remove` is refused. Once the entry has been removed this way, ownership is as follows. A job still in the queue is dropped when it is dequeued. A job already reading the DRAM slot finishes, then frees the slot and the extent it has just written, since nothing references either any more. In that case `remove` MUST NOT free the slot itself. A job whose pin was not taken over settles normally (`convert_to_storage`, or `release_read` if the write failed).

edits.old: it is refused while the entry is pinned or write-locked. Then the memory-tier slot is freed, then the SSD extent (if any). A remove that is refused because the entry is pinned returns `KeyNotFound` and frees nothing.
edits.new: it is refused while the entry is pinned or write-locked. The one exception is the pin of the key's own pending write-through, which `remove` takes over instead (FR-018). Then the memory-tier slot is freed, then the SSD extent (if any). If the write-through job is reading the slot at that moment, the job frees the slot when it is done instead. A `remove` that is refused because a reader or a client `pin` holds the entry, or because the entry stays write-locked past the dispatch-map wait, returns `KeyNotFound` and frees nothing. *(Sync 2026-10-14, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-clear-mt` — code authoritative, commit `0236a3c98`.)*

edits.old: This method evicts ALL entries from the memory-tier pool by calling `IMemoryTier::evict_next()` in a loop until empty. For each evicted key, it transitions the dispatch-map entry to BlockDevice state via `convert_memory_tier_to_block`. If the transition fails (write-through not complete), the entry is removed from the dispatch map entirely. Returns the number of entries cleared.
edits.new: This method empties the memory-tier pool by repeatedly scanning `IMemoryTier::oldest_keys(64 + p)`, where `p` is the number of entries left pinned on the previous pass, so that pinned entries cannot hide clearable ones behind them. For each key it first tries `IDispatchMap::try_evict_to_block` (write-through complete and unpinned → BlockDevice). If that fails for any reason other than `ActiveReferences`, the entry has no SSD copy and is removed from the dispatch map (`dm.remove`). The memory-tier slot is freed (`IMemoryTier::remove`) only after the dispatch-map entry is BlockDevice or gone. An entry that is pinned, by a lookup, a client `pin` or the write-through's read reference, MUST keep its slot and is retried on a later pass, whether `try_evict_to_block` or the `dm.remove` detects the pin: its dispatch-map entry still points at the slot, and the pin holder may be copying from it. A pass that clears nothing waits 50 µs before the next pass. Once 5 s have passed since the call started, the next pass that clears nothing MUST return `DispatcherError::Timeout` and leave the still-pinned entries resident. `Ok(n)` therefore means the tier was emptied, and `n` counts only the entries actually demoted or removed. *(Sync 2026-10-14, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-clear-mt` — code authoritative, commit `cccfb328e`. Previously any failed demotion freed the slot unconditionally, so a pinned entry's dispatch-map entry pointed at released memory, the entry stayed in the map, and the count included it.)*

edits.old: The background writer holds a read reference on each entry while write-through is in progress. The reference is released after write completes or fails.
edits.new: A write-through job queued by `copy_gpu_to_memory_completed` holds the read reference that `downgrade_reference` left on the entry while write-through is in progress. The reference is released after the write completes (`convert_to_storage`) or fails (`release_read`), unless `remove` has taken it over first (FR-018). A job queued by `schedule_write_through` (interfaces FR-031a) is enqueued without a read reference of its own. *(Sync 2026-10-14, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-clear-mt`. This is a known gap, not a guarantee: such a job still settles through `convert_to_storage`, which decrements whatever read reference is held at that moment. A code alignment is tracked in `.specify/sync/align-tasks.md`.)*

edits.old: | `Timeout` | `lookup`, `remove` | Dispatch map blocking operation exceeds timeout |
edits.new: | `Timeout` | `pin`, `clear_memory_tier` | `pin`: the dispatch-map wait for a writer exceeded its timeout. `clear_memory_tier`: the tier could not be emptied within 5 s because entries stayed pinned, and those entries remain resident *(Sync 2026-10-14, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-clear-mt`: `lookup` and `remove` never return `Timeout`; they report a dispatch-map timeout as `KeyNotFound`)* |

which is a miss *(Sync 2026-09-28)*. **For `remove`, also** an entry held by a reader's or client's pin, or one still write-locked when the dispatch-map wait times out; in both cases nothing is freed. The pin of the key's own pending write-through does not refuse `remove` (001 FR-018) *(Sync 2026-10-14, branch `fix/dispatcher-remove-clear-mt`)* |

edits.old: /// Acquires a write reference, then removes the dispatch map entry.
edits.new: /// Removes the dispatch map entry first, then frees the memory-tier slot. The removal is refused while a reader or client holds a pin; the pin of the key's own pending write-through is taken over instead (001 FR-018).

edits.old: - `remove()` guarantees the dispatch map entry is removed when it returns.
edits.new: - `remove()` guarantees, when it returns `Ok`, that the dispatch map entry is removed, so no new lookup can obtain its memory-tier pointer. When it returns `KeyNotFound`, nothing was freed.
